text:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that combines a
retrieval system with a language model. Instead of relying only on
what the model learned during training, RAG first searches a
knowledge base for relevant text chunks, then feeds those chunks to
the language model as context before it generates an answer.

A typical RAG pipeline has the following stages: loading raw
documents, cleaning and preprocessing the text, splitting the text
into smaller chunks, converting each chunk into a vector embedding,
storing those embeddings in a vector database, retrieving the most
relevant chunks for a given question, and finally prompting a
language model with the retrieved context to produce a grounded
answer that can cite its sources.

Replace this file with your own documents in data/raw/ (.txt or
.pdf files), then re-run the pipeline scripts in order from
01_documents.py through 05_create_chroma_store.py.
